title: Exciting skies above the ELT
caption: Construction of the Extremely Large Telescope under the night sky, Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This view of the construction site of ESO's Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) comes from one of the webcams that watch over it. Taken on 3 May 2025, it shows how far building work has come, with the frameworks of both giant dome doors, which will open at night, now in place.

On the far right, a bright orange glow rises into the sky. These are lasers, and although they seem aimed at the meteor to the left, they have a gentler job. They belong to the adaptive optics system of ESO's Very Large Telescope, making artificial guide stars that help correct for atmospheric turbulence and sharpen astronomers' images.
The lasers make sodium atoms glow in a layer of the upper atmosphere about 90 km above the ground. Those atoms were deposited there by meteors, much like the one in the frame.

understand.summary: This is a webcam photograph of the ELT construction site at night, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The webcam's exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the laser beams and meteor streak are recorded more clearly than a person might see them.

explore: When it is finished, the ELT will also use laser guide stars, six of them, to help it deliver very sharp images of the cosmos. The webcams let ESO follow the telescope's progress day and night.
alt: A large dome under construction at night, with an orange laser glow on the far right and a meteor streak on the left.
